label: How we work
heading: Five steps from discovery to post-launch
intro1: When we start a project, we talk less about what we will do and more about what we won't. The five steps below frame the decisions we make, from the proposal stage to post-launch support.
intro2: The order never changes; the duration does. We would rather shorten a step than skip it, because a skipped step always comes back as the cost of the next one.

steps.title: We read the system
steps.body: Before we start building, we look at what is already there: which objects have been written and where each rule is defined. The organization's naming and development standards are taken as inputs.

steps.title: We draw the scope and the boundaries
steps.body: Which data will be accessed, what will be automated and what will go through human approval are settled before the contract. Role-based access is the first design decision.

steps.title: We build under production conditions
steps.body: From day one we design for failure cases, retries and the rollback path. Integration is not left for later; the connection exists in the prototype too.

steps.title: We deliver with evidence
steps.body: For every output, you can see which document, record or rule it came from. Code, configuration and the reasoning behind decisions stay with the organization.

steps.title: We measure after launch
steps.body: We track usage: who uses it, where they give up and at which step they turn back. Updating the solution when rules change is part of the plan.

example.label: What we mean by step four
example.avoidQuote: The system decided this invoice should go for approval.
example.preferQuote: The invoice amount deviates from the purchase order; the relevant clause of the expense policy sends records above this difference for approval.
example.closing: The difference changes how the user behaves: in the first case there is no option but to approve; in the second, a real decision can be made.
